label: GO step, choosing a2 after a rewarded visit to S2 (episode trials < 70)
explanation: Fires only at the GO step (never D1 or D2), and only when the agent is about to choose a2 (model_act == 2, policy logit strongly favouring a2; ~0 activations with a1) right after the previous trial was rewarded. Holding prev_state != 1 (the reward came from S2, or the previous trial is outside the window) raises precision from 0.82 to 0.90. A rewarded visit to S1 followed by an a2 choice is mostly silent. The feature also goes silent late in the episode: it is active through about trial 65, falls off near 70, and is zero for trials 80-99, so ep_trial < 70 is part of the predicate. action at GO is the agent own upcoming choice (equivalent to model_act == 2, same F1), so no future random outcome is used. Excluding a prev_action == 1 trial would add about 1 point of F1, but I left that clause out for simplicity. It does not fire after unrewarded trials or on a1 choices. Magnitude: in the example windows it tends to be higher during streaks of rewarded a2/S2 trials and where the a2 logit is most extreme (the choice bin below -8.9 holds 63% of the mass), but I did not check this beyond those tables.

issues: The core claims hold up. Activation appears only at GO (D1 and D2 are 0/380619 steps each). 75530 of 75557 activations are on action==2, with only 27 on a1. On prev_reward==0 it is active on 205 of 401340 steps. If the previous trial was a rewarded visit to S1, a following a2 choice is silent: precision 0.008, mass recall 0.00003. The late-episode cutoff is real: trials 70-79 have 1408 activations and trials 80-99 have none. Dev precision/recall/F1 reproduce at 0.905/0.977/0.940, and the test F1 of 0.932 reproduces.

The label overclaims with 'after a rewarded visit to S2'. When S2 was reached by a rare transition from a1 (prev_action==1, prev_state==2, rewarded) and the agent then switches to a2, the predicate is true but the feature is mostly silent: dev precision 0.173, recall 0.007, mass 0.003, 3219 predicted steps. That is a systematic false-positive class, not noise. The feature tracks a2 being repeated after a rewarded a2 -> S2 (common) trial, not any rewarded S2 visit. The other agent noticed this clause but left it out. Adding it raises test F1 from 0.932 to 0.946 (precision 0.893 -> 0.926).

The magnitude claim was not tested, and it misses the main magnitude trend: magnitude falls steadily over the episode, not just at trial 70. Each bin of trials 0-9 to 20-29 holds about 10-21% of the activation mass. Trials 50-59 have almost as many active steps as 10-19 (11520 vs 11587) but only half the mass (0.106 vs 0.210). Trials 60-69 hold 0.045 of the mass from 9564 active steps. Within trials 60-69 the predicate covers 13% of active steps but only 4.5% of the mass, almost all in the lowest activation quartile.

Remaining false positives show the feature lags the evidence. The first rewarded a2/S2c trial after a run of unrewarded trials, or when good==S1, is often silent: with good==1 precision is 0.62, against 0.93 when good==2. This suggests the feature integrates evidence over trials rather than responding to a single previous reward. Adding good != 1 or a two-trials-back reward clause lowers test F1 (0.916 and 0.892), so I did not add one. It is a minor systematic gap.
Future variables: the predicate uses only the agent's own upcoming action plus observed history, so uses_future=false is correct.
